rows.label: Value of water-fetching time saved, as a share of consumption, per person reached by water work

source.title: UNICEF, 'Collecting water is often a colossal waste of time for women and girls', press release, 29 August 2016 (WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme data)
source.quote: In sub-Saharan Africa, one roundtrip to collect water is 33 minutes on average in rural areas and 25 minutes in urban areas.
source.note: A household without water nearby makes a trip or two a day, about 180-365 hours a year, 35-75 hours a person in a household of about five. A new or repaired point nearby saves part of that, and water trucking, hygiene kits and repairs to existing systems save less: about 15 hours a person a year across the work (5-40). An hour valued at a year's consumption over a 2,000-hour working year: 15 / 2,000 = 0.75%, from 0 (no time saved, or time with no other use) to 3% (long walks, time valued at the full wage).

rows.explainer: Bringing water closer saves households fetching time, mostly women's and girls': about half an hour a trip in sub-Saharan Africa (WHO/UNICEF). Across the water work aid agencies do (new and repaired points, trucking, hygiene), about 15 hours a person a year, valued at consumption per working hour: 0.75% of a year's consumption (0-3%). Read by every model of ours that values time saved by water supply.
